description: Training or evaluation data written by a model instead of collected from real use.
Generating variations from real examples (rewording, new names, other languages) so the synthetic data stays close to the real distribution.
A method (Wang et al., 2022) where a model expands a few seed tasks into many new instructions and answers, which are then filtered.
Degradation when models train recursively on generated data: rare cases vanish first, then outputs narrow. Avoided by keeping real data in the mix.
The generator's preferences (topics, names, dialects, viewpoints) dominating the dataset and growing stronger in the trained model.
Training data overlapping the eval set (exact or near duplicates, or shared generator phrasing), inflating scores without real gains.
Recording where each example came from (real or synthetic, generator, prompt version, date) so it can be audited, reweighted or removed.
